name: CA-35
label: Safe D

key_factors: Torres holds a roughly 90-to-1 fundraising advantage ($885K raised vs. $9.8K) with $364K on hand
Incumbent Democrat in a D+6 district with a favorable political environment
Prediction markets price Torres near-certain at 98 percent

model.rationale: Every available signal aligns: Torres's overwhelming financial edge, incumbency, the district's Democratic lean, and markets pricing her at 98 percent leave Cargile with no visible path. With no polling to contradict the fundamentals, the expected margin stays near twenty points for Torres.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending for Cargile or credible polling showing a single-digit race would be the main signal that this is tightening.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Norma Torres, the Democratic incumbent, enters the general election as a heavy favorite in a district that leans Democratic by six points. She has raised roughly $885,000 and holds about $364,000 on hand, while Republican Mike Cargile has raised under $10,000 with less than $500 available. No outside groups have invested meaningfully in the race, and prediction markets price Torres's chances at about 98 percent.

The fundamentals point the same direction: incumbency, a strong financial edge, and a favorable political environment combine for an expected margin near twenty points. With no public polling of the contest, the outlook rests on these structural advantages, which show no sign of strain. Cargile would need an outside shock to make this competitive; the evidence available points to a comfortable Torres victory.
